newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany under more pressure not to deport Bosnians.
newsitem.headline: Germany under more pressure not to deport Bosnians.

text.p: Interior ministers from Germany's 16 regional states came under renewed pressure on Thursday to drop their policy of deporting Bosnian refugees if they failed to return home of their own accord.
About 800 Bosnians and their supporters took to the streets in Berlin to protest against the controversial policy.
German officials say it has hardly been enforced. They say about 200 have been deported, some of them convicted criminals.

The United Nations' UNHCR refugee agency called on the ministers, holding a two-day meeting in Bonn, to let refugees from ethnically-cleansed areas now occupied by other groups stay in Germany until it was safer for them to return home.

But Gerhard Glogowski, the interior minister from Lower Saxony, rebutted criticism of Germany's forcible repatration policy and lashed out at Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel for failing to do more to facilitate the refugees' return.

Glogowski said the main problem faced by German states, which took in some 320,000 refugees during the 1992-95 war, was getting the Bosnian authorities to cooperate. He accused Sarajevo of obstructing refugees' return.
He told ZDF television that more than 50,000 refugees had returned voluntarily, but criticised the Bosnian authorities, saying they "don't want to take their own people back, but want our money".
"Why doesn't Kinkel explain to his European counterparts in unequivocal terms what exactly needs to be done so that the refugees can return home safely?" Glogowski asked.
Kinkel and federal Interior Minister Manfred Kanther have been at loggerheads since last October when interior ministers agreed to go ahead with the controversial repatriation policy.
Kinkel argues against deporting refugees from areas that were ethnically-cleansed.
